title: Out-of-equilibrium relaxation dynamics of the superconducting order parameter in CsV$_3$Sb$_5$
authors: Avi Shragai, Alexander Won, Jonathan M. DeStefano, Andrea Capa Salinas, Ganesh Pokharel, Stephen D. Wilson, B. J. Ramshaw
abstract: The application of a time-varying strain field drives a superconducting order parameter out of equilibrium. How the order parameter relaxes back to equilibrium depends both on the structure of the superconducting gap and on the nature of quasiparticle scattering. We report the discovery of an ultrasonic attenuation peak inside the superconducting state of the kagome superconductor CsV$_3$Sb$_5$. This peak is the natural consequence of the order parameter relaxation time matching the ultrasonic drive frequency near $T_{\rm c}$. From the measured frequency dependence of the peak, we extract a microscopic scattering time of $τ_N = 25$ ps. This timescale is two orders of magnitude longer than the elastic scattering time as determined by resistivity measurements, but is comparable to the inelastic scattering time determined by thermal transport. Within the conventional framework of order-parameter relaxation, this implies that elastic scattering is ineffective at relaxing the superconducting condensate, consistent with a sign-preserving $s$-wave state obeying Anderson's theorem.
summary: This paper uses ultrasonic attenuation measurements on the superconductor CsV3Sb5 to study how its superconducting order parameter relaxes after being perturbed. By fitting the data to the Landau-Khalatnikov model, the authors extracted a characteristic scattering time of 25 ps. This result suggests that the relaxation is governed by inelastic scattering, implying that simple elastic scattering processes are ineffective at damping the superconducting condensate.
main_problem: The study investigates how the superconducting order parameter relaxes back to equilibrium after being driven out of equilibrium by a time-varying strain field.
main_result: The authors discovered an ultrasonic attenuation peak in CsV3Sb5, successfully modeled by order-parameter relaxation, yielding a scattering time (25 ps) inconsistent with simple elastic scattering mechanisms.
method: The primary method involves using pulse-echo ultrasound to measure the ultrasonic attenuation ($\alpha$) across the superconducting transition temperature.
model_or_system: The system is the kagome superconductor CsV3Sb5. The dynamics are analyzed using the Landau-Khalatnikov (LK) model, which describes attenuation when the relaxation timescale ($	au_\Delta$) matches the inverse drive frequency ($\omega$).
key_observables: Ultrasonic attenuation ($\alpha$) as a function of temperature and ultrasonic frequency ($\omega$); the relaxation time $	au_N$.
important_parameters: The extracted microscopic scattering time $	au_N = 25 	ext{ ps}$; the comparison between $	au_N$ and elastic/inelastic scattering times.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the applicability of the Landau-Khalatnikov model, requiring $	au_\Delta$ to be comparable to $1/\omega$.
figures_summary: Figures show the crystal structure and strain effects (Fig. 1); the fractional change in the longitudinal modulus (Fig. 2); and the key comparison of sound attenuation, showing a frequency-dependent peak in CsV3Sb5 versus monotonic behavior in RbV3Sb5 (Fig. 3).
paper_structure: The paper develops the theoretical framework using the LK model, applies it to experimental ultrasonic attenuation data on CsV3Sb5, extracts the characteristic scattering time $	au_N$, and interprets this time by comparing it to other known scattering mechanisms (resistivity vs. thermal transport).
why_interesting: The analysis of non-equilibrium dynamics using the LK model provides a concrete example of how order parameter relaxation can be probed experimentally, linking macroscopic measurements (ultrasound) to microscopic scattering physics, which is relevant to open quantum systems.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Crystal structure and experimental strains. Crystal structure of CsV3Sb5 is shown on the left. In our experimental geometry, sound propagates along the crystal c axis and probes the compressional modulus c33 and the shear modulus c44. The atomic displacements associated with the c33 and c44 strains are shown on the right.

FIG. 2. Longitudinal elastic modulus jump at Tc. a, Fractional change in the longitudinal modulus c33 of CsV3Sb5 across its superconducting transition. b, Corresponding fractional change in c33 of RbV3Sb5. The fractional discontinuity is significantly smaller and sharper in RbV3Sb5 compared to CsV3Sb5. We attribute the rounding of the jump in CsV3Sb5 to a combination of strain broadening of the superconducting Tc, and relaxational effects on the sound velocity (Supplementary Figure 8 shows data from 0.46 GHz to 2.44 GHz).

FIG. 3. Longitudinal sound attenuation near Tc. a, Shows the temperature evolution of sound attenuation in CsV3Sb5 at different ultrasonic frequencies. Sound attenuation is peaked just below Tc at low frequencies—this peak decreases with increasing frequency and disappears entirely above ∼2 GHz. b, In contrast with CsV3Sb5, the sound attenuation in RbV3Sb5 decreases monotonically below Tc, conforming to the expectation for a BCS superconductor.

FIG. 4. Fit to the data with the LK model. Fit to the data using the sum of order-parameter-relaxation and BCS quasi- particle contributions. Opaque traces are the model, and semitransparent traces are the data. a, Shows the full temperature range and b, shows a narrower range of temperatures near Tc, as indicated by the bounding box in a. From the LK model, we extract a characteristic timescale for the order-parameter relaxation to be τN = 25 ps.
